{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Elizabeth Lee Wilmer''' is an American mathematician known for her work on [[Markov chain mixing time]]s. She is a professor, and former department head, of mathematics at [[Oberlin College]].{{r|oberlin}}

As a 16-year-old high school student at [[Stuyvesant High School]] and captain of the school mathematics team, Wilmer won second place in the [[Regeneron Science Talent Search|Westinghouse Science Talent Search]] in 1987, for a project involving [[graph coloring|3-coloring of graphs]].{{r|nyt|lat|z}} The first-place winner that year was also female, marking the first year that the top two prizes both went to women.{{r|ap|dw}} As an undergraduate at [[Harvard College]], she led the university's team{{r|TheMathStudent}} that won the first [[Mathematical Contest in Modeling]] of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], and she was one of the two inaugural winners of the [[Alice T. Schafer Prize]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] for excellence by a woman in undergraduate mathematics.{{r|schafer|gallian|MathEducation}} She graduated from Harvard in 1991, and completed her Ph.D. at Harvard in 1999.{{r|oberlin}} She worked with [[Persi Diaconis]] for her doctoral dissertation, ''Exact Rates of Convergence for Some Simple Non-Reversible Markov Chains'',{{r|mg}} but after Diaconis moved from Harvard to Stanford in 1997 her official [[doctoral advisor]] became [[Joe Harris (mathematician)|Joe Harris]].{{r|harvdis}}

With David A. Levin and [[Yuval Peres]], Wilmer is the author of the textbook ''[[Markov Chains and Mixing Times]]'' (American Mathematical Society, 2009; 2nd ed., 2017).{{r|mcmt}}

As of September 2022, Wilmer is a rotating program officer at the National Science Foundation in the Probability program.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 31, 2023 |title=NSF Appoints New Statistics Program Directors |url=https://imstat.org/2023/03/31/nsf-appoints-new-statistics-program-directors/ |access-date=October 15, 2023 |website=Institute of Mathematical Statistics}}</ref>
